knowledge:
- key_parameters: fast5files=A vector containing the path names of the fast5 files to be read ;; attribute=In layoutPlot(), takes 'nreads', 'kb', or 'signal' to plot total reads, cumulative bases, or median signal per channel ;; zValue=In channelHeatmap(), specifies the intensity metric (e.g., 'd2_count', 'd2_prop') with which each channel is plotted ;; zScale=In channelActivityPlot(), a data.frame containing read 'id' and a metric column (e.g., 'median_signal') to color-code channel activity ;; only2D=In plotKmerFrequencyCorrelation(), a logical switch to choose between using template/complement strands (FALSE) or consensus 2D sequences (TRUE) ;; strand=In fast5toFastq(), defines which strands to extract; can be any combination of 'template', 'complement', '2D', 'all', and 'both' ;; ncores=In fast5toFastq(), specifies the number of CPU cores to use for extraction
- alternatives: ShortRead::writeFastq() is used to write FASTQ files from a pre-loaded Fast5Summary object, whereas fast5toFastq() is preferred for direct extraction from raw files on disk without loading them into R memory.
- when_to_use: Use this package when performing quality control, performance diagnostics, and data extraction on Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing runs (FAST5 format).
- pitfalls: Small numbers of reads with extreme values can compress the colors on the z-axis in channel activity plots. Increasing ncores in fast5toFastq() may not significantly speed up extraction because the process is often I/O bound rather than CPU bound. Basecalling failure can result in empty FAST5 files or files with event data but no called bases, which affects slot population in Fast5Summary.

workflows.name: minion_quality_control
workflows.intent: Read FAST5 files, summarize their contents, and generate various quality control plots.
workflows.stages: 1. List FAST5 files ;; 2. Read summaries using readFast5Summary() ;; 3. Extract basecalled data using baseCalled() ;; 4. Plot read accumulation and active channels using plotReadAccumulation() and plotActiveChannels() ;; 5. Plot read categories and qualities using plotReadCategoryCounts() and plotReadCategoryQuals() ;; 6. Plot event and base production rates using plotEventRate() and plotBaseProductionRate() ;; 7. Generate flow cell layout plots using layoutPlot() ;; 8. Generate custom channel heatmaps using channelHeatmap() ;; 9. Plot channel activity over time using channelActivityPlot() ;; 10. Plot k-mer frequency correlation using plotKmerFrequencyCorrelation()
workflows.code:
fast5files <- list.files(path = "/path/to/data/", pattern = ".fast5$", full.names = TRUE)
example.summary <- readFast5Summary( fast5files )
baseCalled(s.typhi.rep1)
baseCalled(s.typhi.rep1[1:2])
p1 <- plotReadAccumulation(s.typhi.rep1)
p2 <- plotActiveChannels(s.typhi.rep1)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
p1 <- plotReadCategoryCounts(s.typhi.rep1)
p2 <- plotReadCategoryQuals(s.typhi.rep1)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
p1 <- plotEventRate(s.typhi.rep1)
p2 <- plotBaseProductionRate(s.typhi.rep1)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
p1 <- layoutPlot(s.typhi.rep1, attribute = "nreads")
p2 <- layoutPlot(s.typhi.rep1, attribute = "kb")
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
read_count_2D <- baseCalled(s.typhi.rep1) %>% ## start with base called reads
  filter(strand == 'template') %>% ## keep template so we don't count things twice
  left_join(readInfo(s.typhi.rep1), by = 'id') %>% ## channel stored in @readInfo slot, match by id column
  group_by(channel) %>% ## group according to channel
  summarise(d2_count = length(which(full_2D == TRUE)), ## count those with full 2D status
            d2_prop = length(which(full_2D == TRUE)) / n()) ## divide by total count of reads from channel
p1 <- channelHeatmap(read_count_2D, zValue = 'd2_count')
p2 <- channelHeatmap(read_count_2D, zValue = 'd2_prop')
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
z_scale = select(eventData(s.typhi.rep3), id, median_signal)
channelActivityPlot( s.typhi.rep3, zScale = z_scale )
plotKmerFrequencyCorrelation( s.typhi.rep3, only2D = FALSE )

workflows.name: extract_fastq
workflows.intent: Extract basecalled sequences from FAST5 files and write them to FASTQ format.
workflows.stages: 1. Extract FASTQ from a pre-loaded Fast5Summary object using fastq(), fastqTemplate(), fastqComplement(), or fastq2D(), and write using ShortRead::writeFastq() ;; 2. Alternatively, extract FASTQ directly from FAST5 files on disk using fast5toFastq()
workflows.code:
writeFastq( fastq( s.typhi.rep1 ), file = tempfile() )
writeFastq( fastq2D( s.typhi.rep1 ), file = tempfile() )
fast5files <- system.file('extdata', 'example.fast5', package = "IONiseR")
fast5toFastq(files = fast5files, fileName = "test", outputDir = tempdir(), strand = 'all', ncores = 1)
